# Expected excerpts for Delaware HB 230 (Grants-in-Aid, FY 2026).
# Each non-comment, non-blank line is an EXACT substring assertion:
#   "<text>"  → MUST appear in the extractor output
#   "!<text>" → must NOT appear in the extractor output
# Whitespace is significant.
#
# Four bugs this fixture locks in:
#
#   1. 2026-06-29 — visual line-order: tabular rows authored with the
#      "$" sigil drawn AFTER the number but positioned LEFT of it were
#      emitted as "<number> $".  Fixed by _sort_block_lines_visually()
#      sorting same-row lines by leftmost x.
#
#   2. 2026-06-29 — visual column gaps: tabular rows authored without
#      whitespace-filler "spacer" lines (DE / IN / KS style) had their
#      310+pt cell gaps collapsed to a single joiner space, jamming
#      columns together.  Fixed by inserting proportional whitespace
#      when same-row x-gap > COLUMN_GAP_PAD_MIN_PT.  The forbidden
#      excerpts below catch any regression that re-collapses the
#      columns.
#
#   3. 2026-06-29 — intra-tag currency padding: dollar amounts that the
#      PDF authoring tool padded for right-alignment (e.g.
#      ``[D>$          236,308<D]``) were carrying the padding into
#      the tag's interior.  Fixed by _RE_CURRENCY_PADDING in
#      _clean_tagged_text, which collapses runs of 2+ whitespace
#      between "$" and a following digit to a single space.
#
#   4. 2026-06-29 — position-based column alignment: gap-based padding
#      placed the dollar column at a DIFFERENT output column for every
#      row depending on label length, so the table didn't read as a
#      grid.  Fixed by computing target_col from each sibling's PDF
#      x-position; every row's "$" column now lands at the same output
#      column.  Long-label rows that would overflow the target column
#      get COLUMN_GAP_MIN_SPACES = 6 spaces of cell separator (raised
#      from 4 → 6 for wider visual gap on long org names in DE tables;
#      ≥ 4 survives the "2-3 → 1 space" collapse in _clean_tagged_text).

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Required: row labels + their tagged dollar amounts.
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Plain row: County Seat Package label + amount on the same physical
# row.  After the position-based padding fix the cell separator is
# exactly 6 spaces (the COLUMN_GAP_MIN_SPACES floor — Package's label
# is too long for target_col = 27 to fit, so MIN kicks in).
County Seat Package      $ 3,880,543

# "TOTAL - Office of the Secretary" full row wrapped in one [A>…<A] tag
# after consolidate_adjacent_tags.  Currency padding inside the tag is
# now collapsed to a single space.
[A>TOTAL - Office of the Secretary $ 3,880,543<A]

# Three-cell row (label + $ + amount) all wrapped in one [A>…<A] tag.
[A>Paramedic Program Operations Block Grant $ 3,000,000<A]

# Senior centres table — verify the row LABEL and the FULL
# [D>…<D] [A>…<A] amount portion appear (multiple rows so that a partial
# column-padding regression is caught).
Absalom Jones
Brandywine
Chesapeake & Delaware
Cornerstone
DeLaWarr
Howard Weston
Mid-County

# The tagged amount portions — single space between "$" and the digits,
# stable regardless of how much column-pad whitespace sits before the
# tag.
[D>$ 236,308<D] [A>$ 245,225<A]
[D>$ 280,642<D] [A>$ 290,446<A]
[D>$ 180,158<D] [A>$ 187,498<A]
[D>$ 151,965<D] [A>$ 158,741<A]
[D>$ 261,465<D] [A>$ 270,431<A]
[D>$ 504,931<D] [A>$ 525,511<A]

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Required: position-based column alignment.  Each row's "$" column
# lands at the SAME output column regardless of label length.  The
# exact space count between label and "[D>" is what makes the table
# read as a grid in plain-text view.  If the algorithm regresses to
# gap-based padding, these will fail because every row's pad count
# will be different.
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Short label (13 chars) → wide padding so "[D>" lands at the target
# column.  Locks in the position-based alignment for short labels.
Absalom Jones            [D>$ 236,308<D] [A>$ 245,225<A]

# Long label (21 chars) → label overflows target column, so the
# COLUMN_GAP_MIN_SPACES = 6 separator kicks in.  Locks in the
# minimum-separator floor.
Chesapeake & Delaware      [D>$ 180,158<D] [A>$ 187,498<A]

# Long-label One-Times row with BOTH [D> and [A> on the same physical
# row.  Same 6-space MIN separator applies.
Kind to Kids Foundation      [D>$ 250,000<D] [A>$ 200,000<A]

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Forbidden: prior buggy forms that the latest fixes were designed to
# prevent.  If any of these reappear, the corresponding regression has
# resurfaced.
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Pre-column-padding-fix form: single space between the entity name and
# the [D>$ amount.  After the column-padding fix the gap is 12 spaces
# (Absalom) or 4 spaces (long-label rows).
!Absalom Jones [D>$

# Pre-column-padding-fix form for the County Seat Package row.
# (1-space form would be collapsed by _clean_tagged_text's 2-3 space
# rule — we explicitly forbid that.)
!County Seat Package $ 3,880,543

# Two-space form for County Seat Package row.  If COLUMN_GAP_MIN_SPACES
# regresses to 2, this is what would appear after _clean_tagged_text
# collapses it to single space; but the MIN must stay ≥6 so the
# separator survives the collapse.  Note: this 2-space form CANNOT
# actually appear because _clean_tagged_text would collapse it — but
# guarding it as forbidden documents the invariant.
!County Seat Package  $ 3,880,543

# Pre-column-padding-fix form for the Brandywine row.
!Brandywine [D>$

# Pre-column-padding-fix form for Kind to Kids Foundation (long-label
# One-Times row): single-space form collapsed by _clean_tagged_text.
!Kind to Kids Foundation [D>$

# Pre-currency-padding-fix form: wide whitespace between "$" and the
# number inside a tag.  Two-space form is the absolute minimum the bug
# could produce; if it ever shows up again the fix has regressed.
![D>$  236,308
![A>$  245,225
![D>$  280,642
![A>$  3,880,543<A]
